title: Mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) measures the average amount of hemoglobin in a single red blood cell. It is one of the red blood cell indices reported as part of a complete blood count.
context: MCH is used together with other red blood cell indices and blood tests to help tell apart different types of anemia. One index alone is not enough to make a diagnosis.
aboveRange: A higher amount of hemoglobin per cell, which can be associated with anemia caused by a vitamin B deficiency
belowRange: A lower amount of hemoglobin per cell, which can be associated with iron deficiency anemia
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
